verdicts.reason: Meta’s own Marketing API authorization guide uses the OAuth 2.0 Login dialog to request ads permissions, which is the primary flow for third‑party apps. ([developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/get-started/authorization))

verdicts.quote: “If your app will be used by anyone without a Role on the app… it must first undergo App Review.”
verdicts.reason: Production use beyond app roles requires App Review, matching the “app_review” access classification. ([developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/resp-plat-initiatives/individual-processes/app-review))

verdicts.quote: “This is a full list of root nodes for the Facebook Marketing API…”
verdicts.reason: The reference shows many resources (ad accounts, campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, audiences, insights, etc.), indicating broad coverage. ([developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/reference/v27.0/))

verdicts.quote: “The ads MCP server is a Meta-hosted Model Context Protocol server… The server is remote-hosted at ‘https://mcp.facebook.com/ads’.”
verdicts.reason: Meta publishes and hosts an official MCP server for Ads. ([developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-overview))

verdicts.quote: “Limited access (default)… For development only. Not for production apps…” and “Advanced access must be approved through the App Review process…”
verdicts.reason: You can self‑serve dev credentials and build now, but production requires App Review/Full Access and is rate‑limited otherwise—hence “ready_with_caveats.” ([developers.facebook.com](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/get-started/authorization))
